'''''Star Wars Zero Company''''' is a [[canon]] single-player [[Wikipedia:Turn-based tactics|turn-based tactics]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] that takes place during the [[Clone Wars]]. The game is developed by [[Bit Reactor]] in collaboration with [[Electronic Arts]]'s [[Respawn Entertainment]] and published by EA and [[Lucasfilm Games]], and  was released on [[August 27]], [[2026]].

==Plot summary==
<!-- This section only follows the required missions. Optional things like the Sawtooth mission are to be documented in the Gameplay section -->
===The Serolonis Operation===
On [[Coruscant]], [[Republic Intelligence]] [[Lieutenant]] [[Bennic Halloren]] and [[Ore-duke|ore-baroness]] [[Jae Mordant]] discuss the growing number of seceding planets during the [[Clone Wars]], and the recent [[battle of Serolonis]], agreeing that it's time to make their move against the [[Infinite Coil]]. They discuss [[Tesh Keff Hawks]], a former [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] [[captain]] who had been [[Hawks' court-martial|discharged]] after the [[Battle of Antine]] and created an independent [[mercenary]] crew named [[Zero Company]]. Mordant admires their skills, but Halloren is unsure about unsavory members of Hawks' crew. Mordant convinces him, since they are running out of time to stop the Coil, and the two prepare to recruit Zero Company.

Over [[Serolonis]], a massive battle is fought between Republic and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] forces. [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry]] [[Starship|ships]] fly by, where the [[clone trooper]]s inside are ready to "blast some [[clanker]]s." Meanwhile on the [[planet]], a [[tragglemouse]] is startled by a shootout, as nearby Hawks runs away from and blasts a [[B1-series battle droid]]. Four Zero Company operators are undertaking a [[Serolonis job|mission]] to retrieve a [[holopuck]]. Their leader Hawks, the [[Cloning|clone]] [[trooper]] [[Trick]], and mercenary [[Phlan Phlolo|Phlan "Aurelio" Phlolo]] hold their position while [[Athlete|fighter]] [[Kabbney Uppercut]] attempts to cut open a [[metal]] safe with a [[blowtorch]]. To buy Uppercut some time, the three fight against approaching B1 [[battle droid]]s. Hawks blasts one [[droid]], Aurelio attempts one but misses, Trick destroys a second, and the crew destroys two more droids. Uppercut opens the case and is surprised by a [[Messenger]] [[Insect|bug]], who escapes. After making sure there aren't any others, they retrieve the holopuck, though Aurelio spots five approaching Infinite Coil troops. Hawks and Aurelio set up overwatch positions, blasting two who get too close. One cultist pins down Aurelio, but is interrupted after being blasted by Hawks, allowing Aurelio to rush forwards and punch them with a melee strike, [[Death|killing]] them. The two remaining enemies blast Aurelio and down him, though Hawks manages to help the injured Aurelio back up. Trick and Uppercut join in, and the four defeat the remaining cultists.

Zero Company's droid [[M-3VO]] contacts Hawks via comms while [[pilot]]ing the ''[[Caisson]]'', and the two agree for the ship to pick them up from a nearby platform. The crew head to the landing pad, commenting on the battle losing against the Republic. Hawks uses their [[PICO-5 electroscope]] to check out the area, realizing they would have to move a crane to clear the landing pad. Moving through a gate and into a battlefield, where they are confronted by four battle droids and three more [[Enforcer (occupation)|enforcers]]. Aurelio takes out all the droids with an [[impact bomb]], while Hawks asks Trick for backup, the two work together to blast a troop. Uppercut takes out another one by shooting an explosive container, and then the crew kills the last one. Heading to the landing pad, they are confronted by four more enemies, one of which turns invisible. Aurelio heads to the [[control panel]] to move the crane out of the way, but immediately after doing so the invisible striker re-appears, hitting Aurelio with a [[club]] and killing the [[Rodian]]. Hawks shoots the striker and Trick fires a [[Missile launcher|rocket launcher]], defeating three of the Coil members. After the fourth is eliminated, M-3VO arrives in the ''Caisson'', Hawks asks the droid to bring a [[hover-stretcher]] for Aurelio. Upon arriving, the [[medical droid]] M-3VO says there is nothing he can do for Aurelio, and Hawks solemnly says Aurelio was a good operator who knew the risks.

They spot one surviving Coil enforcer, who declares himself of the Coil and infinite, telling Hawks that [[Kundri Fathom|Fathom]] will show their destiny, and declaring that he has a fate other than death, before dying in front of the crew. Not wanting to be around if more Coil members appear, Hawks decides the crew should leave Serolonis. Hawks, Trick, Uppercut, M-3VO, and Aurelio's body fly in the ''Caisson'' back to [[the Den]], a [[bulk freighter]] docked to the [[Ring of Kafrene]] and Zero Company's headquarters.

===In Debt to the Hutts===
After docking, Hawks is in their office, preparing a beverage and checking their [[datapad]], which has the mission results on the Serolonis job. [[Runa Blask]] enters and tells Hawks that she can't continue working in these conditions. Hawks, initially misunderstanding, says if the problem was with the [[refresher]], Uppercut promises it won't be an issue again. Blask isn't talking about that, and says Zero Company is running out of [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]], how their rent is coming up and they are losing clients. Even after Hawks points out the holopuck they collected from Serolonis, Blask tells Hawks that it won't cover the massive debt they have with the [[Hutt Clan]], reminding them that making a deal with the [[Hutt]]s was a bad idea in the first place. Hawks tells Blask that Aurelio died, which annoys Blask now that they have to hire a new mercenary, even though they have no credits due to their overwhelming debt. Hawks attempts to reallocate resources, they acknowledge Blask's annoyance and affirm they are working on getting the money. Hawks jokes that not paying Blask would save a lot of money as she heads out of the office towards the [[holotable]].

Hawks follows Blask, passing by their fellow operators and a [[Hologram|holographic]] memorial for Aurelio. The two begin a hologram call with [[Gorga Desilijic Aarrpo]]. Gorga hopes Hawks can cover their debt, and offers a job to forgive some of the money, bringing their debt down to 80,000 credits. Hawks accepts, and Blask points out that the debt is rapidly growing to an unsustainable amount, to which Gorga offers for Blask to work for him when Zero Company fails. Gorga ends the call, reminding the crew that he is only so patient. Hawks undertakes an operation to tail Gorga's clerk [[Bruckner]], who Gorga suspects is working with rivals. On [[Nal Hutta]], Zero Company follows Bruckner to a [[Comm station|comm terminal]] and discovers he is sending confidential information off-planet. Gorga was unhappy to learn this, however Bruckner fled to the planet [[Nevarro]], Gorga hired Zero Company to again hunt him down, where they discover him drunk in a [[skyslum]]. Upon realizing his situation, Bruckner reveals his Republic transmit codes and that he has been sharing information on Gorga to the Galactic Republic. Zero Company makes their decision and deals with Bruckner, successfully completing their operation.

Next, Gorga hires Zero Company to deal with [[pirate]]s who have been stealing from his [[Outer Rim Territories]] [[Smuggler|smuggling]] warehouses. The pirates are in a ghost town on [[Lothal]], so Hawks, Trick, and Uppercut undertake this [[Skirmish on Lothal|mission]], flying off in the ''Caisson''. They arrive in the town where it is raining, and immediately begin a fight against the pirates. There are four initially, but are soon reinforced by two more who emerge from a nearby building. The crew successfully eliminate the outlaws and return to the Den. Zero Company receives 1,000 credits for completing Gorga's mission.

In the Den, Hawks visits the Personnel Facility, a holographic display for managing the operators, and engages in friendly cross-training between operators. Next, Hawks visits the [[Armor]]y which is run by the [[Lasat]] [[Neesh Renark]], and equips a [[medpac]] on their person. Hawks then visits the holotable where Gorga offers the crew two missions: to raid a Separatist outpost on [[Kaller]] for equipment he claims, or to collect tech from outlaws on [[Dantooine]]. The crew make their choice, which Gorga congratulates on their good taste, and looks forward to hearing the mission is completed. Hawks, Trick, and Uppercut travel to the planet in the ''Caisson'', where they face enemy forces and use a safecracker on a security chest, which gets it open. They collect the goods before evacuating, and receive credits for the job.

===The Infinite Coil Investigation===
Hawks returns to their office, where they meet Jae Mordant, she reveals herself as the employer for their Serolonis operation. Hawks gives her the holopuck, and Mordant says she'll pay the crew before offering another job. Bennic Halloren enters. Hawks is hesitant by the Republic's presence and the initial deception, Halloren reveals the puck belongs to the Infinite Coil, a paramilitary [[terrorist]] group affiliated with the Separatists and run by Kundri Fathom, where all the members have some sort of [[disease]]. As the Coil infiltrates Republic territory, this allows the [[Confederacy military]] to follow. Mordant reveals her home [[Luunata]] was taken over by the Coil and she joined the [[Hunt for Kundri Fathom|operation]] on the Coil. Halloren uses the holopuck to reveal Fathom's next target is [[Courtsilius]], an [[ecumenopolis]] in the [[Hosnian system]]. He offers Zero Company a job, to help them investigate the Coil, in exchange for their help and money. Hawks initially turns them down, hesitant to work with the Republic again given their past. Halloren offers to help Zero Company escape their debt to the Hutts; Hawks responds by asking Halloren to double the offer, which is accepted. Halloren sets up his work at Zero Company's holotable, and Mordant comments on a medal in Hawks' office before exiting too, joining Zero Company's operators.

Hawks speaks to Halloren at the holotable, who pays Hawks for the Serolonis job as well as an advance for their [[Mission to the Gressan Breakbulk Dockyard|mission to Courtsilius]]. This is more than enough to pay off their debt with the Hutts, which Hawks is grateful for. Blask tells Hawks to visit the Upgrade Facility, a [[Viewscreen|holoscreen]] used to track building upgrades and maintaining the Den. Hawks spends 1,000 credits to order the supplies Renark needs to operate a [[black market]] facility within the Den. Next they check the Recruitment Facility, a [[computer]] used to track independent contractors. Hawks spends 500 credits to hire one to join Zero Company as an operator. Back at the holotable, Hawks pays off their entire debt. Gorga was shocked by Zero Company having so many credits, but said it didn't matter how it happened, knowing Zero Company will eventually need more money, and says they can always come into his employ again. Afterwards, they follow Republic intel on the next Coil mission. Halloren briefs Hawks and Blask about Courtsilius; despite being a prominent trade center, the undercity has very little resources to get by. He says the Coil plans to meet local [[gangster]]s at the [[Gressan Breakbulk Dockyard]]. Halloren asks Zero Company to investigate what they're up to, wanting them to do so with stealth. Hawks jokes that "quiet" is their middle name, Blask says that it is actually Keff, something that Blask was apparently asked not to tell anyone about. Hawks gets the conversation back on track and says to get a team together.

Hawks and three other operatives fly to Courtsilius in the ''Caisson'', arriving at the dockyard. Hawks and the others investigate the place, however their path is cut off by three [[Slugrats]] who tell them the road is closed and to get going. Instead, the team searches for another path, Hawks uses a [[computer spike]] to slice open a door, commenting that they learned the skill on [[Nar Shaddaa]]. They make their way to the docks, where Hawks sees [[Visser]] on a [[boat]] full of cargo, telling the Slugrats to distribute it planet-wide on behalf of Fathom. Mid-conversation, Visser realizes their methods were indiscreet, as he spots Hawks spying on them. He leaves with the cargo, and tells the remaining Slugrats to dispatch Zero Company. The four succeed in defeating the smugglers. Hawks contacts Halloren and concludes the Coil is running a big shipping operation with the Slugrats' help. Although Visser left with the cargo, a manifest datapad was left behind which mentions the [[Toco-Po Toy Company]]. Halloren tells them to return to the Den, and the crew flies back home.

Hawks revisits the holotable, and they discover that an associate [[director]] of the [[Trade Federation]] who led a failed coup against [[Nute Gunray]] fled from [[Cato Neimoidia]] to Kafrene. They have been broadcasting a signal offering information in exchange for Republic asylum. Blask is interested in the fact of a recent defector. Halloren suggests they aid the Republic with the information, though Blask is unconvinced. The different operators weigh their opinions on how to respond to the situation, and Hawks makes their decision with how to handle the defector. Next, Hawks checks their map to check their contacts, allies of Zero Company assigned to various zones of [[the galaxy]], helping the crew's influence. Hawks sends a contact to Zone Jenith, and the increase in influence earns the crew 2,500 credits. Next, Hawks checks on the manifest they collected from Courtsilius, which has thousands of pieces of data info mentioning the Slugrats importing mysterious cargo from the Toco-Po Toy Company. Further investigation reveals the company is a shell corporation tied to the Separatists, but the crew still needs more time to analyze the files for any connection to the Infinite Coil. While waiting for this to finish, Zero Company undertakes another job, sending four of their operators in the ''Caisson'' to the location. Zero Company is confronted by battle droid forces on the ground but succeeds in completing their mission and returns to the Den.

Zero Company has found information in the manifest, which Hawks is reviewing at the holotable. An Infinite Coil transmission frequency is hidden in the files, which is sliced into so the team can track encrypted transmissions. Indeed, after doing so the team detects Coil activity, a message sent out by Visser which they trace to a secret training facility that is susceptible to sabotage. The crew continues to search for leads on Courtsilius, and in the meantime undertake another mission with four of their operators. They fly to the location aboard the ''Caisson'', where they encounter enemy forces on the ground. Nevertheless, the crew successfully completes their mission and returns in the ''Caisson'' to the Den.

===The Shadow Plague===
Having gathered enough intel from the datapad, Zero Company decides to send a team to the Courtsilius undercity to learn more about the Coil. They gather intel from people in the undercity, and learn that the Coil's leader Kundri Fathom plans to visit Courtsilius, in a cavern system under the [[Takali Canal]]. Bennic Halloren comments that this is the first major lead on Fathom, and Blask questions what she looks like. Halloren begins his briefing, telling Blask and Hawks that Fathom will soon head to the caverns under Courtsilius's undercity. He says the caverns can be entered via a lock at the Takali Canal, where the team can intercept Fathom. He hopes Zero Company can capture Fathom, though Blask and Hawks would also be fine if she is killed. Hawks and three other operators take the [[Mission to the Takali Canal|mission]] and fly to Courtsilius. Upon arriving, they search for the lock in the undercity. When they reach the canal, they are confronted by seven Slugrat enforcers; the team needs to drain the canal to enter the tunnel. During the ensuing battle, they use a console to do so, though the Slugrats are reinforced by five more enforcers. In the end, Zero Company manages to defeat the remaining Slugrats. Hawks leads the team into the tunnels, as they explore they discover several unconscious guards, and eventually reach the caves. 

Once there, Hawks encounters [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Tel-Rea Vokoss]] who is already spying on the Coil. Fathom, alongside Visser and [[ST-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid|super tactical droid]] [[Typhon]], begins an initiation. She tells civilians that if they lost all hope, she has a way to provide. She says there is a central power behind everything; while Fathom says the upper class does not care about their struggles, Hawks tells Halloren that they have a visual but can't risk shooting her because of the civilians. Halloren tells Hawks to stand by, meanwhile Fathom calls out the Republic for hypocrisy, glorifying the Separatists and tells the converts that they might have a place in the Infinite Coil. When one of them appears unsure, she recognizes their fear and attempts to reassure them, urging them to become part of something greater. She says she offers truth and power, and reveals five Messengers in a bowl in front of her. She brings the bugs to two people, saying perhaps they are destined to join or destined to die, and her [[Shadow Plague]] will reveal the truth. After being bitten, one dies from the plague, but the other survives, now with visible markings on their head. Now able to feel the plague's power, Fathom welcomes them into the Coil, as part of the Infinite. Hawks is shocked by what they see, Vokoss reveals that the survivors of the plague are taken to be trained as part of the sect. Fathom tells the cultists to test the others. Visser dismisses them as weak and unwilling, however Fathom reminds Visser, her son, that he was once like this but has grown more formidable, Visser should be able to inspire them. As most of the cultists leave, Hawks says to Vokoss that they have a chance to free the remaining people, and Vokoss offers to help, [[the Force]] is her guide. Hawks tells her to evacuate the converts while Zero Company fights the seven remaining Coil forces. As Vokoss does so, Zero Company engages in battle against the Coil. They discover that, upon a Coil unit's death, the Shadow Plague calls out and surges the capabilities of nearby hosts. As they fight, the cultists are reinforced with five more members, including a stronger Coil Brute. After killing the forces, Hawks investigates the battlefield, and Vokoss returns after having evacuated the citizens.

Hawks comments that they weren't expecting Jedi presence, and Vokoss reveals she has spent the past [[Standard month|months]] tracking the Coil. Hawks introduces themself and questions what Fathom is up to, Vokoss explains that the Coil offers greatness but actually infects those converts with the Shadow Plague, a disease transmitted by the Messenger creatures. The plague kills many, but those who survive grow stronger, with enhanced healing and resistance to pain. Fathom is the central figure, who claims she can hear the plague's voice, and the cultists are unwaveringly loyal to her. Realizing the scale of the threat, Hawks offers Vokoss to join Zero Company, however she declines. She accepts a communications device, Hawks says they will contact her if they find anything notable, and ask her to do the same. Vokoss wishes Hawks good luck and heads off. Hawks inspects the Messenger's bowl one last time before stepping away. Flying the ''Caisson'', Zero Company returns to the Den.

Hawks is at the holotable, where Vokoss sends a lead for the team. Having spoken to the converts, she learned the Infinite Coil plans major work on Courtsilius to get the planet to join the Confederacy. Zero Company shares what information they know, and asks her for a follow-up about the operation. She is thankful for the info, and mentions the mysterious cargo they have been using the Slugrats to import on-planet. She says there are thousands of these crates, and is searching for the main distribution center and will contact the team once she finds out more. Afterwards, they detect Coil activity on two different worlds, where they plan improvements to their forces. While waiting for Vokoss' further intel, they embark on another mission with four of their operators, flying to the location aboard the ''Caisson''. Upon arriving, they encounter enemy forces on the ground. Despite the opposition, the crew successfully completes the mission and returns to Kafrene aboard the ''Caisson''.

===Shadows of Umbara===
While they wait for Vokoss to report back, Zero Company decides to investigate her, curious why a Jedi would be on this mission. They send two operators and contact someone on Coruscant, who reveals that Vokoss is the padawan of [[Salveren Hadrix]], a [[Jedi Knight]] who had been reported as missing in action along with Vokoss over a [[Standard year|year]] ago. Vokoss then contacts Zero company, revealing the Slugrats are distributing out of a warehouse in the [[Threetower District]] that had been abandoned by a textile company. Vokoss and Hawks agree that investigating the warehouse is key to uncovering what the Coil is up to. Halloren identifies a service tunnel the team can infiltrate to enter the warehouse. Four operators, including Hawks, undertake the [[Mission to the Threetower District|mission]] and travel back to Courtsilius. They arrive and Halloren remotely points them toward the warehouse entrance. Hawks identifies the Slugrats crates and, once they get close enough to the entrance, are confronted by seven smugglers. As they clash, the Slugrats are reinforced by five more. Zero Company eliminates them and enters the warehouse, and Vokoss contacts Hawks revealing she has also just entered. Hawks spots them moving lots of cargo, and a hologram of Fathom on a [[mechno-chair]] is speaking to a Coil Marauder, saying [[Count of Serenno|Count]] [[Dooku]] will be pleased with their progress. She leaves, saying she has an appointment with the [[Umbaran|Shadow People]], meanwhile Hawks spots Vokoss sneaking around the facility. She opens one of the crates, and is attacked by eight battle droids who were inside the cargo. Vokoss defeats the droids with her two [[lightsaber]]s but this alerts the Coil to the intruders, she and Zero Company engage in battle against Coil forces. Six Coil and six B1-series battle droids attack the team, and as the battle goes on a [[droideka]] emerges from a crate. It is then joined by reinforcements, another four B1s and three Coil soldiers. After eliminating all forces, Hawks shows the battlefield to Halloren via hologram, while Vokoss examines Fathom's mechno-chair. Halloren suspects the droids were smuggled on-planet for a planned Separatist invasion. He tells Hawks he has already alerted the authorities, who plan to deal with the battle droids now that they know about their presence.

Halloren is glad for the Republic's success, to which Hawks jokes that, when they were discharged, [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] called them an "abject disgrace to the Republic." Halloren mentions he will mention it in his report, but they are interrupted by Vokoss recovering Fathom's hologram, her message from earlier saying she will meet with the Shadow People. Halloren recognizes the Shadow People are Umbarans, who are Separatist, to which Hawks points out that the Republic [[Battle of Umbara|retook]] [[Umbara]]. Halloren speculates the Coil might be planning to sabotage this, and offers Hawks more work. Vokoss questions Hawks' connection to the Republic, which they answer vaguely. Vokoss wonders why they were called an abject disgrace, and Hawks asks why Vokoss and her Master were listed as missing in action. Hawks reassures her that he didn't tell the [[Jedi Order|Order]], and Vokoss reveals that Hadrix was killed by the Shadow Plague after realizing it was bigger than an ordinary disease. She doesn't want to be reassigned, afraid that it won't allow her to continue her work, to finish the job she started, so she has stayed hidden while on the hunt for Fathom. Hawks wonders if this has made Vokoss lonely, regardless of her [[Jedi training]], and offers her to join Zero Company, that their collaboration could end the Coil much faster than either of them alone. Vokoss accepts and joins Zero Company, and afterwards the team returns home.

Zero Company decides to investigate Fathom's connection to the Umbarans. Hawks assigns a team of two operators to listen into Umbaran communications, and learns that Fathom is working with [[Umbaran Partisans]], a group that has been fighting against the [[occupation of Umbara]]. They also intercept a Coil transmission from Visser, which they trace to a secret battle droid upgrade factory that is susceptible to sabotage, which would give the team an advantage in fighting against the sect. As the team continues to investigate [[Rhy Cesca]] who is the leader of the Partisans, they embark on another mission with four of their operators, flying to the target location aboard the ''Caisson''. On arrival, they encounter enemy forces on the ground. Fighting against them, the crew is successful in completing the mission and they return to their base at Kafrene aboard the ''Caisson''.

As Hawks checks the mission results on a datapad, Neesh Renark enters the office and says Hawks has a visitor. Although Hawks says they are busy, Renark disagrees and the [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Clytemnestra Kullervo|Clytemnestra "Cly" Kullervo]] enters and introduces herself. Hawks has heard of Kullervo, and questions why she is there. She offers to join Zero Company; they both realize her asking price would be too high, but she isn't in it for the money. She wants access to Zero Company's information network. She has targets she wants to eliminate, and wants Zero Company's help in doing so. Hawks questions who these targets are, but Kullervo doesn't answer. Though Hawks has questions, they accept and hires Kullervo. Kullervo joins,<ref name="ClyDB">{{Databank|cly-kullervo|Cly Kullervo}}</ref> though does not want an official contract. Hawks welcomes her onto the team. Afterwards, Hawks goes to the holotable. There, they are faced with a dilemma, where Hawks has to make an important decision. The different operators give opinions on how to resolve it, and Hawks makes their decision with how to handle the situation. After the outcome, the team returns to their investigation on Rhy Cesca. Since Cesca is a formidable fighter and former diplomat, her connection with Fathom is concerning for the Republic. To gather intel on Cesca on Umbara, they choose an approach and learn that she has been in contact with both the Coil and [[Executive Separatist Council]], and is heading to a secret meeting with Republic delegates. Before Zero Company can act, the team needs time to investigate the meeting. In the meantime, they embark on another mission with four of the operators. They travel to their destination and, once there, fight against enemy forces. The team completes their mission and returns back to the Den.

===The Attack on Storm Basin===
As Zero Company researches Cesca who plans to head offworld, the team suspects Fathom plans to [[Attack on Storm Basin|sabotage]] the secret meeting. Despite their research, the team cannot find the location of the meeting. Even Halloren is unsure because of its classified nature. The team decides to ask a more dubious source, and this contact discovers that the meeting is a [[prisoner]] exchange that will take place on [[Storm Basin]], a [[mining]] [[City|colony]] of the planet [[Bespin]]. They also informed the team about Coil activity elsewhere, the opportunity for a targeted strike against the cult that could help weaken it. Zero Company needs time to scout Storm Basin to be able to infiltrate it, and while they do this, another mission is undertaken where they fight against more opponents. They are once again successful in this mission and return to Kafrene.

Tesh Hawks checks the holotable where the team has intercepted another transmission from Visser that is led to a secret Coil factory, where their central computer is susceptible to being sliced into for sabotage. On [[Bothawui]] Zero Company contacts the [[Bespin Wing Guard]] about the upcoming Separatist attack, acting as independent security contractors and requesting to access the meeting room. They tell the Storm Basin security that there is a threat to people, however the [[chief]] dismissed the warning, claiming that Bespin is very safe, especially Storm Basin. During the meeting, the team also stole a guard uniform. Bennic Halloren describes to Hawks and Runa Blask that Storm Basin is a supplier of [[tibanna]] [[gas]], and the location of the upcoming meeting between Republic delegates and Rhy Cesca's Umbaran Partisans. The partisans have been fighting against the ongoing Republic occupation of Umbara. The meeting is a prisoner exchange, which surprises Blask. Halloren explains that the Infinite Coil is targeting the exchange, and also that Cesca has been in contact with the Coil and Separatist Council. They assume that the plan is to sabotage the exchange, recover the prisoner and attack the Republic [[ambassador]]s. Halloren thinks the guard uniform should help Hawks sneak into the place. Hawks thinks they would look good in the uniform, and they are sent in alone to Storm Basin.

Upon arrival, Hawks speaks to Halloren over communications. They pass by a worker, who assumes Hawks is a guard and gets to attention, Hawks tells them to at ease. Hawks asks Halloren how their disguise was, which he affirms and asks Hawks to deactivate the comm. Hawks uses a [[turbolift]] to reach the station lobby. There, they notice a security checkpoint in front of another lift, so they get to high ground and use their electroscope to spy on the guards. They overhear a conversation confirming that nobody is allowed in, under direct orders by [[Major]] [[Striker (Bespin)|Striker]], to which another guard comments that Striker has been taking advantage of his promotion. Hawks returns and speaks to the guard captain, pretending that Striker needed them to enter for one last security check. The captain is unsure, Hawks repeats the statement about Striker milking his promotion, and is allowed into the turbolift which takes them up and they head to the room. Entering, they see Rhy Cesca, an [[Umbaran soldier]], and the clone [[troop]]er prisoner [[Dozen]]. Cesca looks at Hawks, who stands back.

At the other side of the chamber, the Jedi [[Anakin Skywalker]] enters with an Umbaran prisoner, [[Luco Bronc]]. Skywalker also notices Hawks, but is interrupted as Dozen speaks up. Skywalker angrily hopes the Umbarans haven't been starving Dozen, to which Cesca points out that the Republic occupation has been starving Umbara, and the prisoners have received the same rations as the soldiers. Skywalker wants to get the exchange over with, Bronc and Dozen trade places, Bronc rudely bumps into Dozen expressing his distaste. Dozen's [[Stuncuffs|binders]] are removed by Skywalker, who is happy to see him back. Cesca releases Bronc, then the two Umbarans express their love and kiss, which Hawks and Skywalker exchange comments on, establishing that Bronc killed many Republic soldiers. Suddenly, the doors close and the lights flicker which concerns Hawks, Skywalker questions who they really work for. Hawks begins to explain he was contracted by Republic Intelligence to hunt Fathom, who suddenly appears in front of everyone in a large hologram. She expresses her distaste for the Republic, which she believes is already broken and clinging to life, that it cannot be negotiated with. As she speaks, she is backed up by four [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle|''Sheathipede''-class transport shuttles]] outside the [[Viewport|window]]. Fathom reveals the Separatist Council prohibited this prisoner transfer, and Cesca went against their wishes, so the Separatists intend to kill her for this.

The room prepares for conflict as Fathom declares the station will fall, and an [[HMP droid gunship]] flies into view, firing through the [[glass]] into the room. Skywalker uses the Force to get himself and Hawks to cover, however Dozen is caught in the fire and killed, as do Cesca and the Umbaran guard. Bronc cradles Cesca's body and laments his fallen lover as the [[gunship]] flies closer. Skywalker brandishes [[Skywalker lightsaber|his lightsaber]], and four Coil soldiers enter the room. Hawks, Skywalker, and Bronc - who wields a [[sniper rifle]] - battle against the Coil. The Coil are reinforced by three more who exit a ship, and afterwards another four who enter the room. The impromptu team kill the enemies, and afterwards look around the battlefield. Skywalker inspects Dozen while Bronc leaves a promise to Cesca's body. Hawks contacts Halloren, asking where the remaining Coil ships are heading, and Skywalker questions who Hawks is and about Fathom's identity. Hawks introduces themself, and that Fathom is the leader of the Infinite Coil, a Separatist paramilitia. They warn Skywalker that Fathom's claim of taking down the station is a very real threat. Halloren informs Hawks the Coil is targeting the [[reactor]] at the base of Storm Basin, Skywalker and Hawks realize Fathom plans to blow it up, and agree to stop this. Bronc joins too, now wearing an Umbaran [[helmet]], and with the intention of fighting more of the sect.

The three take a turbolift to the grand lobby, and discover the place is in ruins: six people are in danger, while two Coil and two [[BX-series droid commando]]s are also in the room. The three decide to rescue the civilians before it's too late. Though two additional Coil join the fight, they manage to rescue all of them and defeat the Coil enemies. They see outside the window, a nearby station exploding and falling. Skywalker mourns the losses that they were too late to help, and recognizing that this is what happens when the reactor is blown, the three hurry to the turbolift. They rush to a platform where the Coil has planted their explosives, eight cultists are present alongside two BX [[commando]] [[sniper]]s and an HMP droid gunship. As the three work to disarm the explosives, the gunship bombards the area with its deadly [[Missile|rocket]]s, while the enemies are reinforced by another soldier and BX commando who arrive by ship, then later another soldier and BX commando. Hawks, Skywalker, and Bronc work together to disarm all four explosives and save Storm Basin, defeating the cultists on the platform. Afterwards, Skywalker leaps onto the droid gunship intent on destroying it. One final Coil soldier fires at him, but Bronc snipes them. Skywalker uses his lightsaber to slash the droid lander, crippling it as he slides back to the platform, while the gunship falls into an explosion. The three walk away from the battlefield, Skywalker and Bronc are impressed with each other's work.

Later, at another landing pad, Skywalker speaks to Hawks again. He affirms what Hawks said was true, though is surprised since he had never heard of work like Zero Company before. Hawks says the point is to be secretive, and Skywalker says they need more independent thinkers like Hawks, how that is a skill that separates them from droids. He says this will help the Republic win the war, Hawks hopes Skywalker is right. Skywalker wishes them that [[may the Force be with you]], and enters in a Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry ship. Bronc approaches Hawks, knowing they are after Fathom, and offers to join. Hawks points out Zero Company sometimes works with the Republic, which is fine with Bronc, however he jokingly says he doesn't intend to call Hawks "sir." Hawks chuckles, saying Bronc would fit in with the team. As Skywalker's [[transport]] flies away, the two walk off, and eventually take the ''Caisson'' back to the Den.

===The ''Ossic Hand''===
While Hawks checks their datapad, Tel-Rea Vokoss enters and tells Hawks they have a visitor. Hawks is initially dismissive, but straightens up when they realize it is Anakin Skywalker, asking how they can help. Skywalker reveals he looked into the Infinite Coil himself, and found information that Salveren Hadrix collected on the Shadow Plague. The Jedi declared Hadrix and his padawan, Vokoss missing in action and presumed dead. Vokoss affirmed that the plague killed Hadrix, however Skywalker is curious why Vokoss never returned. Vokoss thinks the Jedi didn't believe in her capabilities, saying she never would've been a padawan without Hadrix's work. With Hadrix gone, Vokoss worries the Jedi will reassign Vokoss, making her unable to continue her mission against the plague. She joined Zero Company in order to fight the plague. Skywalker asks Hawks if this is accurate. Hawks responds, and Vokoss questions if Skywalker intends to bring her back to the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]], though Skywalker says he and the [[Jedi High Council|Jedi Council]] don't always agree. He gives Vokoss a [[holocron]] with all of Hadrix's research, hoping this could help her efforts. He intends to give Vokoss some time, however hopes that Vokoss does eventually return to Coruscant. Vokoss promises she will, and Skywalker says it is important for one to follow their own path, and for the Force to be with her. Skywalker stays on the Den for the [[cycle]], while Hawks heads to the holotable to continue the hunt for Fathom, who has disappeared after Bespin. The team gathers leads, including one about the Coil planning to upgrade their battle droids, with operations on two separate worlds. Bennic Halloren needs some time to look through the info on the Coil, and as he does this, the team continues their work in pursuing the sect. Zero Company completes another mission where they fight enemy forces. They emerge victorious from the trip, and return to the Ring of Kafrene.

As Hawks exits their office, Luco Bronc is speaking with the clone trooper Trick. Bronc asks about Umbara, if Trick or any of his friends took part in the battle. Trick says this was after he had left, acknowledges bad things happened, but defended the actions because the clones were just following orders. Bronc is annoyed that this is all Trick can say about the war, about Bronc's friends being killed. Trick points out that many clones also died on Umbara. Bronc revels in this fact, how he remembered the death of many clones, causing Trick to pull his [[blaster]] on Bronc. Taunting Trick, Bronc says he wouldn't dare shoot, calling him a "good clone." Trick fires, the blast shooting right past Bronc's head, surprising him. Trick says he's not that good, and bumps into Bronc as he walks away. Bronc calls back, that Trick can come by any time he's ready to continue, mockingly calling the clone "brother" before walking away too.

Hawks is at the holotable, where more Coil activity is detected. Zero Company traced a transmission from Visser to a training camp which, given decisive action, could be sabotaged. Republic Intelligence has a new job for the team, they reached out to Halloren needing help finding the ''[[Ossic Hand]]'', a Separatist [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]] that has a list of Republic [[Spy|spies]]. Given Zero Company's record and connections, they think this team would be a perfect fit for the operation, which they are also offering a higher payout because of the speed in which the job needs to be done. The crew accepts, and uses their intel network to track it down, finding that the ship is docked on the planet [[Orinda]]. Impressed, the Republic offers the next job: to infiltrate the ship and retrieve the list before it's too late. Halloren gives a briefing to Hawks and Blask, showing a holo-image of the Ossic Hand. They disagree on whether or not the ''Lucrehulk'' has a good design, though Blask points out the cost is efficient. Getting their conversation back on track, Halloren explains they need to recover the list in order to warn these [[agent]]s and rescue them before the Separatists can act on this intel.

They know the ''Ossic Hand'' is receiving maintenance at the [[Orinda Dockyards]], and Zero Company's [[Ambush on Orinda|mission]] is to infiltrate the docks, slice into the [[databank]] and recover the list. The operation needs to be done quickly, as Orinda is a Confederacy planet, which Hawks acknowledges. Their team, Hawks and three more operatives, fly to Orinda. Once they arrive at the docks, Halloren guides them via comms to go to a terminal on another platform. Hawks questions the lack of security, Halloren suggests the Separatists are expecting an aerial attack and not a light infiltration team. Hawks points out that Halloren is one of them too, and reaches the control panel. Hawks accesses the list, then Halloren sends a warning that the Coil is [[Jammer|jamming]] their signal, they know Zero Company is present and they need to get out of there. A hologram of a super [[tactical droid]] activates, and reveals that he expected Hawks to be there, the Coil has been tracking Zero Company's operations against the cult but it will end now. Hawks questions why a tactical droid is taking part in this, instead of serving aboard a [[Providence-class Dreadnought|''Providence''-class Dreadnought]].

The droid introduces himself as Typhon, and says he won't reveal anything that could give Zero Company an advantage. He tells them that he has calculated the Shadow Plague, in fact a singular organism, has the potential to forever change the [[galaxy]]. This was what interested Typhon, which is why he serves Fathom. He questions Hawks' motivations, why someone discharged from the [[Republic Military]] and found success as an independent operator, has now returned to the Republic. Typhon says the odds of Zero Company taking down the Coil are negligible, so why even bother to fight? Hawks suggests it's just a way to pass time. Typhon ends the call, saying Hawks' crew won't escape the planet alive, as three [[Vulture-class starfighter|''Vulture''-class starfighters]] fly overhead. As a large number of battle droids and Coil fighters enter the docks, Halloren tells them to evacuate immediately as the [[droid starfighter]]s prepare attack runs. The team avoids the laser bombardment and, although the enemies receive even more reinforcements, Hawks and the others reach their evacuation point and escape. They then fly back to their base.

===The Road to Luunata===
The next cycle, Hawks checks the holotable where Jae Mordant and Halloren have a new operation. Hawks references the disaster during the ''Ossic Hand'' mission, which Halloren takes the blame for. Hawks points out that Halloren's decisive action and quick extraction saved the squad. He returns the topic to their hunt for Fathom, how they have a new mission to [[Mordant Citadel|Fathom's base]] on Luunata, and crippling its defenses so the Republic can undertake a [[Assault of Luunata|battle]] there. Mordant says how Luunata was her home, which she lost when Fathom annexed the place. She hopes this operation would help her reclaim the planet, so she asks Hawks to please help her. Halloren agrees that this could turn the war in their favor, and will pay Zero Company well. Hawks agrees, that it is time to retake Luunata. They need to find a way to infiltrate the citadel, due to its high defense they need to find an alternative way in. Hawks assigns three operators to analyze the citadel layout, who find there is a path in through the planet's [[Volcano|volcanic]] tunnels. With no other plan, the squad now needs to figure out how to safely fly through a volcano. While they study the [[Magma|lava]] tunnels, Zero Company takes on another mission in the meantime. They once again encounter forces in opposition on the world but are successful in the end, flying the ''Caisson'' back to the Den.

In Hawks' office, they are on a datapad when Cly Kullervo enters, saying that she has her first target, [[Idra Farrar]]. She says the information is with Halloren, who she thinks of as an intern. Kullervo states that it is time for Hawks to uphold their end of the agreement, and help her track down Farrar. The request is responded to by Hawks, who heads to the holotable. First Zero Company has to deal with [[Halas Fang]], a [[senator]]ial [[aide]] for [[Malastare]], who had hired the crew months earlier to deal with [[Coruscanti]] gangsters that tried to extort him. Despite owing Zero Company 1,500 credits, he still hasn't paid up, claiming that he needs more time. Hawks, Halloren, and Blask comment on the situation, and different operators weigh opinions on how to handle this. Hawks made their decision and dealt with the situation satisfactorily.

Hawks reviews their campaign at the holotable. ===Retaking Luunata===
Zero Company makes a deal with [[Klassek II]], an [[ore]]-[[baron]] willing to trade thermal shields in exchange for ore processing equipment from [[Eriadu]]. Since [[Eriaduan]]s do not sell to those offworld, Hawks dispatches a team of three operators to steal the equipment from Eriadu. They do so, and exchange it for Klassek's shields. As they prepare for their assault of Luunata, Halloren says they have always waited for a mission like this, and Blask is mildly disgusted by his enthusiasm. Jae Mordant begins her briefing with Hawks, Blask, and Halloren by showing a hologram of Luunata, a planet she is sentimental about, that she built a mining citadel alongside [[castellan]] [[Kinro Billix]] that rivaled that of those on Shu-Torun. It was taken over by Kundri Fathom for the Separatists, but now Mordant hopes they can take it back. She explains that it has a massive [[drill]] for underground [[minerals]], and the [[turbolaser]]s that defend it from above prevent an aerial assault. As Halloren points out, that is why Zero Company is to infiltrate and take down the defenses. Blask adds the way they'll do it is by flying into a volcano, Hawks jokes about the unpredictability of their missions. Halloren says the plan is to fly below where their [[sensor]]s can't detect and up through the volcanic cracks, where they will use their thermal shields and fly through the tunnels. Blask says the shields better work or they'll all burn up, and Hawks jokes they'd prefer to be buried at [[Ocean|sea]], so they don't mind a sea of [[fire]]. Mordant plans to use a turbolift to enter the citadel, within which they will find a console to shut down the place's defenses. Halloren says the [[Republic Navy|Republic fleet]] is waiting by in the [[Kril'Dor system]], reiterating that when Zero Company takes down the defenses, the Republic can begin their attack, to retake the planet and help take down the Infinite Coil. Mordant agrees, desiring to retake her home and liberate it from the Coil's occupation.

Hawks is ready to begin the mission, so they and three operators travel to Luunata on the ''Caisson'', alongside Halloren and their pilot M-3VO. Flying the ship, M-3VO keeps a low approach to avoid detection, and Halloren points out the fissure which M-3VO enters. Activating the thermal shield, M-3VO flies through the magma tunnels, the two make sure the shield stays stable as the heat around them rises, Hawks keeps their eyes on a hologram tracking their progress. M-3VO reaches the end, and Hawks' team prepares to exit the ship. They wish each other luck, M-3VO pointing out the team needs more luck since he's rated for extreme heat unlike Hawks. Hawks jokes that they're relieved by that as the squad exits the ship. They navigate through the mining tunnels, seeing a massive drill which Hawks is impressed by the size of. They reach the turbolift, but are confronted by eleven Coil enforcers, alongside four battle droids. Even as the enemies receive reinforcements of eight more cultists, the team reaches a control panel to call a turbolift. Unfortunately, the [[Bellhop]] refuses to open the lift, thinking Zero Company are Separatists just like those who took over Luunata. Hawks tries to explain but the Bellhop can't hear them because of the battle. Once they eliminate all the enemies, Hawks heads to the turbolift which finally opens. The Bellhop, a [[protocol droid]], greets them. Learning that Zero Company intends to liberate Luunata from the occupiers, the droid welcomes them aboard and brings the lift to the citadel. Hawks has the team move forward, noticing all the raw ore around them.

They reach a group of guards at the back door, three B1 battle droids, a cultist, and an [[IG-100 MagnaGuard]]. As Zero Company takes them on, four more Coil join the fight. Once they eliminate them all, Hawks slices open the door, and the team enters the citadel. Halloren contacts Hawks over comms, saying that the Republic has begun its attack. Hawks acknowledges, and then activates a control terminal. There, they notice an old security recording which shows Fathom, Typhon, and Visser who is restrained. In the recording, Typhon scolds Visser, accusing him of helping clone prisoners attempt to escape, which Typhon deemed such wasteful deaths since they could have been infected with the Shadow Plague, indoctrinated into the Coil. Visser responds that they would've been unsuccessful if they tried, their torture methods didn't break their training and only made them mad. Typhon disagrees, replying that this was exactly what he was researching. He says that even Visser should understand why clones are so important to the plague's unfolding. Visser says Typhon is only doing this because he likes seeing people suffering, Typhon calls Visser insolent, and Fathom cuts the two off. She scolds Visser for putting everything they worked for at risk. They have finally found a home for themselves, asking if he would rather if they were cast out. He reminds Fathom that she says only the weak are afraid of conflict, but she isn't having it, angrily saying that Visser betrayed her. She doesn't know if he might do it again, if he might leave them. Visser attempts to appeal to her familial connection, saying that he is her son. Typhon says that is the only reason why Visser hadn't been infected, to not risk him dying from the plague. Typhon tells Fathom they were wrong to trust her son, and they need to finish their work. Visser pleads, but Fathom ignores her son. As Fathom prepares to infect him, he says he would never forgive her for doing this. However, she has faith that he will in the end.

Fathom releases a Messenger bug onto him, which bites Visser, infecting him with the plague. As the recording ends, Hawks, who is still watching, is shocked Fathom would do this to her own family. Hawks says it is time to finish their mission. Suddenly, Zero Company realizes the lift has been locked down, and they will need to override it at the terminal. As they work to do so, four Coil enforcers enter the room, who the team needs to fight against. The forces are supported by three B1 battle droids, a MagnaGuard, and another cultist. Then nine more Coil enter the room. Hawks and their team manage to lift the security lockdown, and escape to the turbolift. As they reach a platform, Hawks watches the ongoing battle in the sky, Republic starfighters fighting against the citadel's turbolasers. Hawks spots a lever, which would allow the crew to shut down the Coil's defenses, but as they walk towards it, they get stopped in their tracks by Visser. He tells Hawks to not resist Fathom, as the two exchange blaster shots back and forth. Hawks says they know what Fathom did to Visser, that it wasn't right. Visser says the plague is a gift that gave him purpose and peace. Hawks doesn't believe it was worth the cost. Visser thinks Hawks' cynicism weakens them, Hawks is a strong fighter after all, they could be part of something bigger like Visser is. Hawks says they'll think about it, after they liberate Luunata. Visser, gesturing to more Coil guards, says Hawks' path ends here. The team fights against Visser, who tells his five Coil guards they have Zero Company pinned down, to show what their courage is worth. During the fight, he questions the path Hawks chose, fighting on behalf of a Republic that doesn't care about them. Hawks jokes that it pays well.

Working together, the team takes down Visser and the Coil militants. Once the battle is over, Hawks reaches the turbolaser controls, shutting them all down. Then from a turbolift, Fathom exits with cultists, who she orders to kill Hawks. They fire at Hawks, who tries to contact Halloren that the sky is now clear, but is knocked out by a [[thermal detonator]]. As Hawks gets back up, they are attacked by Visser. Meanwhile, four LAAT/i gunships fly by, firing at Fathom's guards and killing them. Visser reactivates the turbolasers as he struggles against Hawks. While the two clash, three [[clone jetpack trooper]]s exit a gunship. They try to fight Fathom, however she kills them all, taking one down with the Force. Visser pulls a [[knife]] on Hawks, however they use it to destroy the defense system. Hawks shoots Visser dead, which is witnessed by Fathom. The two look at each other, but the arrival of a Republic [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] in the sky prompts Fathom to escape, flying away in a ''Sheathipede'' transport. Halloren contacts Hawks, who picks up their communicator and grins looking out at Luunata.

In the aftermath of the battle, many clones look over the battlefield. Halloren walks up to Hawks, saying he never thought he would miss the Republic's [[ration pack]]s. Hawks jokes that it is a reaction to eating too much of Neesh Renark's [[Foodstuff|food]], to which Halloren questions how old Renark's food even is. Hawks offers Halloren their [[canteen]], and Halloren hands them a ration bar. As they look at the Luunata landscape, Hawks comments the rations aren't as bad as they remember, saying Halloren should request some more for Zero Company. After all, the team helped retake a planet. Halloren agrees the higher-ups are impressed with this work, who offered to promote him to Captain, and would give him oversight on operations like Zero Company's. However, he plans to turn down the promotion, which shocks Hawks. Halloren wants to stay with Zero Company, believing that the team is more successful than any other Republic operations. He believes their work could help improve the galaxy. Hawks disagrees, saying their team doesn't have any political allegiances. Hawks doesn't want anyone sacrificing themselves on behalf of Zero Company, especially not a friend like Halloren. Halloren insists he wants to stay, not seeing this as a sacrifice, but Hawks disagrees. They tell Halloren to look out for themself, and say that these days they don't have much of any firm beliefs. Hawks tells them to accept the promotion once they take down Fathom, it would do the Republic good to have someone smart like Halloren. They just need to finish their job first. Halloren agrees, and Hawks congratulates the soon-to-be captain. As [[fireworks]] go off over Luunata, the two agree they both did good work in this. They return to Kafrene.

===The Fall of the Republic===
Hawks visits the holotable, where Halloren reports that the Republic Navy has swept the [[Luunata system]], and the Separatist occupation has ended. Jae Mordant is happy for Zero Company's work, and hopes that soon she can finally return home. She appreciates everything Halloren has done to help, and Halloren agrees. She promises to stop by Hawks' office before she leaves, and Halloren says they need to act decisively to take down Fathom as the Coil retreats, before she can go into hiding. He plans to bring in an elite clone unit, [[Stillwatch Battalion]], to help take down the Coil. Hawks is unsure how the team might react to sharing space with a clone [[battalion]], but agrees with Halloren that they need the extra firepower, now that the Coil knows they are being hunted down. Although the Republic wasn't able to track Fathom's ship, Zero Company sends a team to [[Ord Mantell]] to see if people in the criminal underworld might know where Fathom is. The team checks the black market for rumors, and talks to an individual who reveals that Fathom and the Coil have fled to the planet [[Aleen]]. This operation also allowed the team to get some upgrades. In the meantime, while they work on tracking Fathom to Aleen, Zero Company takes on another mission against enemy forces. Fathom says this will be the last. She is supported by five cultists and two infected clone troopers. The team battles Fathom and her forces, and finally manages to take her down, killing her. On her body, the plague markings begin to disappear. One of the Messenger bugs crawls by and it also dies. Hawks inspects Fathom's body before sitting back, the markings on their face also vanishing with a relieved expression on their face. Halloren approaches Hawks, asking if they are alright. Hawks confirms, saying that it feels the plague is dying with her gone, that it is finally over. As they stand up, Halloren looks at Fathom's body, before being confronted by two Coil enforcers and two plagued clones. One of the clones says they felt the plague disappear, and now they confirm that Fathom is indeed dead. A Coil agrees, saying that they can no longer hear her voice. The other clone recognizes Hawks and takes off his helmet, revealing himself as Ender, the clone who Hawks encountered on Kaller. Hawks recognizes him, happy to see Ender survived everything.

Hawks confirms to them that Fathom is dead, and everyone is now freed. Ender reflects that he initially thought Fathom freed them, showed the clones that their inhibitor chips controlled them, and made them turn on the Jedi. The other clone reflects that they just traded one enslavement for another. An enforcer asks what they should do now, and Hawks says this is up to them. Ender figures there is nothing left to do here, and offers to assist Zero Company, to which Hawks agrees. Blask calls Hawks, saying Imperial ships are arriving from hyperspace, saying that she and M-3VO will leave with or without the team, which Hawks acknowledges. They tell the formerly infected that Zero Company is heading out, anyone is welcome to join with them. The two clones and an enforcer follow Hawks. The remaining Coil stays behind and walks the other way, which Hawks acknowledges is their choice. Hawks asks if Halloren is coming. He tries to talk, but Hawks cuts him off, saying he has a space in Zero Company if he chooses to rejoin. Halloren agrees, dropping his [[Rank insignia plaque|rank plaque]] on the floor, telling Hawks to lead the way as they walk off and leave behind Fathom's body. Having finally destroyed the Infinite Coil, Zero Company flies back to the Den.

Hawks is aboard the Den, alongside all their fellow operators, including Ender who has now joined the team. Hawks approaches Halloren, who is no longer wearing his [[Imperial military uniforms|ISB uniform]], at the holotable. Hawks says Halloren is the very man they wanted to see, asking if there has been any Coil activity. Halloren says, while the stolen ''Venator'' is still missing, Coil outposts have been abandoned all over the galaxy. He says the cult is finally gone. Hawks tells Halloren to smile, this is a happy occasion. He reflects that, with the Coil gone, this gives space for the Empire to take power now that this obstacle is gone. Hawks says they don't blame Halloren for what happened a year ago. When the Empire rose, the two ended up on opposing ends of a situation where there was no winning. Halloren says that, at the time, he couldn't believe the Republic was actually gone. They believed that the Empire could be fixed from the inside, which is why he was a part of it. He says what the Empire is doing is much worse than can be imagined, the Empire is complicit in countless atrocities and knows it. He reflects that he doesn't know how to live with the fact that he played a role in this. Hawks says he needs to, one way or another. They say he shouldn't be let off the hook, but if he can take those emotions and acknowledge them directly, that is the best path for Halloren to take.

Renark and Blask walk in, Renark saying the team got a call from a known Rodian client with damaged antenna and rebel friends. Blask says the Rodian wants help getting past an Imperial checkpoint within the [[Chommell sector]]. Hawks questions the status of Imperial security, Renark says it's not too much but with all the heat on Zero Company, the Empire would see the team coming. Halloren speaks in, saying he has something, which interests Hawks. He pulls up on the holotable a potential route through an asteroid field, which could allow them to get past the checkpoint. He acknowledges the potential danger, but says they could manage it if the ''Caisson'' flies it. Renark and Hawks are impressed, and Blask jokes that Halloren earned another week for rations. Hawks says Zero Company might now have a career in working against the Empire. Blask is unsure on that idea, but since she already accepted the job, supposes they need to make the credits. Hawks jokes that, now that the team is working for the greater good, they don't intend to pay them anymore. Renark is unamused, then grins as the two fist-bump. Hawks chuckles and says it is time to make some money, then the ship jumps to hyperspace.

==Gameplay==
===Overview===
Similarly to past strategy games from the developers at Bit Reactor, especially [[Wikipedia:Firaxis Games|Firaxis Games]] ''[[Wikipedia:XCOM|XCOM]]'' reboot series,<ref name="PC Gamer 3">{{WebCite|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/strategy/yes-zero-company-really-is-star-wars-xcom-and-its-got-the-permadeath-to-prove-it|text=Yes, Zero Company really is Star Wars XCOM, and it's got the permadeath to prove it|author=Robin Valentine|date=2025-04-19|archivedate=20251114081150}}</ref> the combat is played in turn-based character actions from a [[Wikipedia:Third-person (video games)|third-person perspective]] with additional cinematics in between.<ref name="Full panel" /> Set during the [[Clone Wars]], the game will see players take control of former [[Galactic Republic]] officer [[Tesh Keff Hawks]], a fully customizable character, as they lead [[Zero Company]] on covert missions fighting against [[Infinite Coil|an adversary]] threatening the entire [[The galaxy|galaxy]]. The group will feature a pre-written group of former [[soldier]]s and [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] from diverse and conflicting backgrounds who, like Hawks, can be heavily customized, as well as original custom characters created by the player.<ref name="swcom Update" />

Additionally, a players choice's will influence the direction of the story and the characters can form bonds that will give them powerful combat synergies<ref name="swcom Update" /> and also influence their character development.<ref name="Gizmodo" /> Among other elements, the game features a [[Wikipedia:Permadeath|permadeath]] mode,<ref name="PC Gamer 3" /> an Ironman mode (called [[Beskar]] mode in-game), and the [[The Den|player's main base]] on the [[Ring of Kafrene]] features an expansive and detailed interactive [[map]] of the galaxy.<ref name="swcom Update" />

===Player choices===
====Overview and Hawks' design====
As a highly customizable game, ''Zero Company''{{'s}} story and its in-game dynamics will shift depending on the player's choices, such as what characters survive in permadeath mode and what options a player chooses when talking with their teammates.<ref name="SWZC">''[[Star Wars Zero Company]]''</ref>

At a base level, Hawks is heavily customizable by the player, who can chose the character's outfit, gender, and species. These choices will also impact in-game dialogue; Hawks will refer to themselves as a female or male depending on the player's decision. Further, Hawks will have their voice muffled behind a helmet should a player equip Hawks with one. The same is true if other characters are given helmets.<ref name="SWZC" /> As the vast majority of marketing material<ref name="swcom Update" /><ref name="Gameplay Trailer swcom" /><ref name="Gameplay Trailer">{{EASWYouTube|WxLUZ1omFA8|Star Wars Zero Company | Official Gameplay Trailer}}</ref><ref name="HawksEA">{{EA|url=games/starwars/zero-company/operators-hub/hawks|text=Hawks}}</ref> and Hawks' entry in the [[Databank (2014-)|official ''Star Wars'' Databank]] depict Hawks as a [[human]]<ref name="HawksDB">{{Databank|hawks|Hawks}}</ref> male,<ref name="Gameplay Trailer" /> this article assumes that to be Hawks' [[canon]]ical design. Indeed, this is the depiction the game uses in its opening cutscene, prior to customization.

====Character paths====
{{IncompleteList}}
=====Trick's possible paths=====
======Rescue of Sawtooth======
Early in game, Trick is listening in on Republic comm chatter and presents present the player with an optional mission to [[Rescue of Sawtooth|rescue]] [[Clone Sergeant]] [[Sawtooth]], a surviving member of the 100th Clone Company who now commands a [[Sawtooth's unit|new unit]]. Sawtooth is currently trapped on the [[Fighting on Ryloth|beleaguered]] planet [[Ryloth]], with [[Republic High Command]] unable to offer any support. For old time's sake, Trick asks Hawk to launch a mission to rescue their old comrade. If accepted, Trick will rally Zero Company to the mission, which sees its operators touch down and rescues the captured Sawtooth from battle droids on Ryloth. While departing, Sawtooth has a chance to catch up with Hawks and Trick. While happy to see them, he is disturbed that Trick is no longer serving the Republic directly and that Zero Company, whom he notes are technically civilians, listen in on encrypted Republic communications. He warns he will need to report these actions, to which Hawks explains that Bennic Halloren is up front and will help with that.<ref name="SWZC" />

Following the rescue, as Trick muses over how quickly Sawtooth wanted to get away from him and Hawks, the player is given the choice to ask Trick what he expected or to tell him not to take Sawtooth's attitude personally. If the player chooses the former, Hawks will blast Trick for expecting more in a time of war, telling him not to waste time after Zero Company just spent time on the rescue mission. This option reduces the player's bond with Trick. If the player chooses the latter option, however, Hawks will emotionally connect with Trick, revealing that Hawks understands how Sawtooth must be feeling after losing his unit because of their own experiences with the Battle of Antine. Trick is quick to assure Hawks that the Battle of Antine was not their fault and that they were simply following orders, something which Hawks remarks is not enough to guarantee a good night's sleep. This version of the conversation boosts Hawks' bond with Trick.<ref name="SWZC" />

======Personal debate======
In Cycle 15, after Trick has an argument about the Battle of Umbara with Luco Bronc that culminates in Trick pulling his [[blaster pistol]] on the Umbaran and nearly shooting him, Trick will ask Hawks whether they are sure if having Bronc as a member of the team is a good idea. The player can either have Hawks admit they are not sure—in which Hawks assures Trick that, at least, Bronc seems to hate Kundri Fathom more than he hates the Republic, which Trick hopes to be the case—or tell Trick to just focus on the mission. The former option increases the bond between Trick and Hawks. If the player chooses the latter option, Hawks will simply tell Trick to focus on his work while they handle Bronc, something Trick agrees to. However, this version of the encounter decreases the bond between Hawks and Trick.<ref name="SWZC" />

Towards the end of the Clone Wars, Trick muses as to whether the success of their operation against Fathom will allow him and Hawks to rejoin the Republic. The player can either have Hawks say there is no chance, which Trick admits is "fair enough," or that it is possible, which Trick vaguely answers "would be something." No matter what option is chosen, Hawks will ask Trick how he feels about the prospect, to which Trick admits that he is no longer sure despite having previously longed for that chance.<ref name="SWZC" />

=====Runa Blask's possible paths=====
When [[Runa Blask]] argues against Republic policy surrounding [[Courtsilius]] and uses it as an example as to why planets have joined the Confederacy, the player can either have Hawks argue the Separatists are worse or simply have them back away from the debate by asking Black not to make them defend Republic policy. In the former, Hawks will point out that [[General]] [[Grievous]] and his [[Separatist Droid Army|droid armies]] are not working on the projects Blask would want to see, something Blask admits before mentioning her support of the free market. In the latter, Hawks will simply ask Blask not to make them defend the Republic, to which Blask reiterates her support of the free market. In either option, Hawks ends the conversation by telling her she can believe whatever she wants to in her free time, but right now needs to get back to work.<ref name="SWZC" />

=====Kabbney Uppercut's possible paths=====
After [[Kabbney Uppercut]] informs Hawks about his past with the Pyke Syndicate and tells Hawks not to worry about it, the player can either have Hawks chose to respect Uppercut's boundaries, which increases the bond between Hawks and a grateful Uppercut, or have Hawks tell Uppercut the situation is their concern, with Hawks arguing that the Pykes may target their operators. While Hawks ultimately choses to step back when Uppercut repeats that it is not a problem for Zero Company, this option decreases the bond between Uppercut and Hawks.<ref name="SWZC" />

No matter the case, Hawks will later tell Uppercut they apologize for "[ruffling] some feathers" with how they talked about the Pykes, assuring Uppercut that, if he believes it is not a problem, they will not think of it as one. In response, Ubbercut tells Hawks about his family. If the player does not have these conversations with Uppercut, Uppercut will quickly speed through his history to explain his background to the player when the Pykes finally find his family, surprising Hawks. If the player already had these conversations, Hawks is already familiar with Uppercut's background and family.<ref name="SWZC" />

These dialogues culminate in the player having the optional mission to rescue Uppercut's family.<ref name="SWZC" />

=====Jae Mordant's possible paths=====
One optional mission sees Zero Company rallying on a [[Mission to rescue Kinro Billix|mission to rescue]] Jae Mordant's uncle [[Kinro Billix]], who has actually been infected with the Shadow Plague and lures Zero Company to [[Florrum]]. The mission ends in failure as a result of his infection and subsequent death, a distrust Mordant will blame herself for his fate.<ref name="SWZC" />

In one response option, the player can have Hawks assure Mordant that Fathom is responsible, not her, and ask Mordant to remember that Billix trusted in her, telling her that, now, all she can do is make his sacrifice worthwhile, which she agrees to. In another response option, Hawks will tell the distraught Mordant that they understand the feeling of spending people to their deaths, alluding to the Battle of Antine by saying the cost of leadership is to lose those who trusted in you, which she says she will have to take their word for. No matter which option is chosen, however, Hawks will tell Mordant back at the Den that they do not think Billix would have seen things as him getting sent to his death on her word.<ref name="SWZC" />

=====Tel-Rea Vokoss's possible paths=====
If the player does not join Tel-Rea Vokoss in investigating her lead on other surviving Jedi, which leads to her clash with the Second Sister, she will leave Zero Company to investigate Dantooine on her own.<ref name="SWZC" />

=====Luco Bronc's possible paths=====
In Cycle 15, after Luco Bronc's argument with Trick, the player can approach Bronc, who lambasts Trick for "hiding behind" the excuse that his clone brothers were just following orders. The player can have Hawks respond by telling Bronc not to make trouble, which results in him saying Bronc may need to leave if he intends to cause problems, or assure Bronc that they understand, albeit while telling Bronc that the Den is not the place to resume Clone Wars arguments. In the latter version, Hawks asks Bronc to simply be a member of the team, even if he does not want to be friends with Trick, which Bronc accepts. The former version of events decreases the player's bond with Bronc while the latter increases it.<ref name="SWZC" />

The player has the option to join Bronc in carrying out the [[assassination of Geryon]] on Sullust, in which Zero Company fights through Geryon's droids and corners the unit. While Geryon proclaims he dies in the name of the Confederacy and warns Bronc he will almost certainly not feel better about Rhy Cesca's death by killing him, Bronc answers that Geryon dies for Cesca and decapitates the unit, admitting the execution did not make him feel better afterward.<ref name="SWZC" />

If the player does not join Bronc in carrying out the assassination of Geryon, Bronc will complete the mission on his own offscreen and return upset with Hawks over the lack of help. This choice decreases the bond between Bronc and Hawks. During the epilogue, Bronc will also remind the player that they did not help out in the mission during their final conversation. If the player did join the mission, Hawks recalls during the epilogue that the assassination "was quite a mission."<ref name="SWZC" />

=====Cly Kullervo's possible paths=====
When the [[Mandalorian]] [[Cly Kullervo]] introduces herself to Hawks, the player has the option to accept her offer to join Zero Company or decline. If the player accepts, Kullervo will become an operator available for use with her own storyline of revenge.<ref name="SWZC" /> Kullervo's official Databank entry has confirmed that this is the canonical path in this encounter by affirming that she canonically joined Zero Company.<ref name="ClyDB" /> If the player chooses to turn down Kullervo's offer, [[Neesh Renark]] will speak up and ask Hawks to reconsider, which presents the player with the option for a second time. Should the player still turn down Kullervo's offer, Kullervo will depart while Renark argues with Hawks about the decision, which Hawks defends by claiming the Mandalorian would be more trouble than she was worth. Renark reluctantly accepts the decision but tells Hawks it will fall to them to tell Blask they have turned down the skilled hunter's offer.<ref name="SWZC" />

Later at Renark's black market stand, Renark will repeat his distaste at needing to let Kullervo walk away as Zero Company might never again have such a skilled candidate. If the player did choose to have Kullervo join, this conversation at the stand is replaced by Renark pondering about all the ways he could exploit the Confederacy's supply chain.<ref name="SWZC" /> As Kullervo joining Zero Company is the canonical path,<ref name="ClyDB" /> this article assumes the supply chain dialogue is what canonically happened.

Before release, a preview of ''Zero Company'' provided by a German ''PC Gamer'' article, itself based on in-depth conversations with the developers, dated the events of the game to [[20 BBY]].<ref name="PC Gamer 4 de" /> In the actual game itself, however, references to the [[bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar]] and a [[Atrocity on Mahranee|conflict on Mahranee]] narrow down its Clone Wars-era events to [[19 BBY]].<ref name="Date" />
